shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures fell on Wednesday, pressured by a stronger yen and expectations that raw material cost support will weaken.($1 = 158.1500 yen)($1 = 6.6785 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures fell on Wednesday, pressured by a stronger yen and expectations that raw material cost support will weaken.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for March delivery
was down 3.3 yen, or 0.73%, at 448.8 yen ($2.84) per kg
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 125 yuan, or 0.63%, to 19,685 yuan ($2,947.52) per metric ton
The most active November butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) was little changed at 15,690 yuan per metric ton
held on to most of the previous session's sharp gains on Wednesday, with the greenback little changed at 158.16 yen, after an auction of longer-dated Japanese government bonds drew record demand
A stronger currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers
Thai raw material prices are expected to ease in October, barring unforeseen weather disturbances, weakening cost support for natural rubber, analysts from broker GF Futures said in a note
Tyre production is expected to stay low, with operating rates below the same period in previous years, while spot and social inventories in Qingdao continue to accumulate, the analysts said
Upstream factories' willingness to purchase raw materials at elevated prices has declined, analysts from broker Huatai Futures said in a note
Downstream tyre manufacturers are holding low raw material inventories and continuing to draw down finished product stock, signaling limited acceptance of current prices, the Huatai analysts added
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for January delivery (STFF7) last traded at 251 US cents per kg, down 0.8% as of 0713 GMT
